Done. The kernel at [output_model_new.py](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level1_moonbridge/p39/round0/output_model_new.py) compiles and passes all 5 correctness trials.

**What's in the file:** A single `@avelang.jit` kernel that handles L2 normalization for shape (32768, 65535) in BF16. Each CTA processes one full row — threads do strided accumulation of sum-of-squares, tree-reduce in shared memory, thread 0 computes the norm via `al.sqrt`, and then all threads apply the division in a second strided pass. The host wrapper converts input to BF16 and routes the result back to the original dtype.

**Results:**

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Compiled | true |
| Correctness | 5/5 |
| Runtime (mean) | 5.25 ms |
| Ref runtime (mean) | 4.53 ms |

The ~16% gap mostly comes from reading the input twice within the kernel (once for reduction, once for apply). A fused single-pass approach would need register-caching the strided elements, which exceeds reasonable register budgets at 256 elements per thread. The reference PyTorch kernel likely benefits from MIOpen-level fusion that hides this second pass.
